definition: `Essence F ex φ x w`: φ is necessarily included in every property ψ that x has at w, that is, for each such ψ, at every world accessible from w every existing individual that has φ has ψ (AFP definition Essence, φ Ess. x ≡ ❙∀ψ. ψ x ❙⊃ (φ ❙⊃⇩N ψ), with PropertyInclusion φ ❙⊃⇩N ψ ≡ ❙□(❙∀⇧Ey. φ y ❙⊃ ψ y)). Unlike Scott's essence (DEF-ESSENCE-SCOTT) it does not require x to have φ, so the empty property is an essence of everything (STMT-GOEDEL-1970-EMPTY-PROPERTY-IS-ESSENCE), and its inclusion quantifies over existing individuals only. Not the Thomist essence.
